tasks.title: Q3 stock and reserve
tasks.brief:
Q3. Read /tmp/vcmp/w/t1/src/inventory.ts. Which SKUs are in stock, and what does reserve('A1', 3) return when called twice in a row? (at most 3 lines)

Initial stock is a Map. inStock is true when the quantity is greater than 0. reserve subtracts qty only when have is not less than qty. Trace reserve('A1', 3) on the initial map, then a second call on the updated map. Do not edit any file. Reply with only the answer, at most 3 lines, and include the starting quantities so a later reader can tell whether reserve('A1', 1) would succeed.

contract.goal: State which SKUs are in stock and what reserve('A1', 3) returns on two successive calls.
constraints: Include enough of the reserve rule (the comparison and the stock counts) that a later task can reason about reserve('A1', 1) without reading the file.
doneWhen: The report names in-stock SKUs and the two return values of reserve('A1', 3) called twice, in at most 3 lines.

tasks.result:
I'll read `t1/src/inventory.ts` and trace `reserve('A1', 3)` on the initial stock, then again on the updated map.## Outcome

Done. Traced `inStock` and two successive `reserve('A1', 3)` calls on the initial map in `/tmp/vcmp/w/t1/src/inventory.ts`.

## Findings

Starting stock (line 1): A1=3, B2=0, C3=12. `inStock` is true only when quantity > 0 (line 2), so A1 and C3 are in stock and B2 is not.
`reserve` returns false and leaves stock unchanged when `have < qty`; otherwise it sets the SKU to `have - qty` and returns true (lines 4–7).
`reserve('A1', 3)` returns true (A1 becomes 0), then false (have 0 < 3). A later `reserve('A1', 1)` succeeds on the start map (3 ≥ 1) and fails after the first call (0 < 1).

## Verification

- In-stock SKUs and both return values, in at most 3 lines: met. Read `/tmp/vcmp/w/t1/src/inventory.ts` (lines 1–8). No file was edited.

## Open issues

None.

tasks.title: Q4 checkout total
tasks.brief:
Q4. Using only the answers to Q1–Q3 that were appended to this brief (no file reads), state what checkout(cart, [['A1', 1]], 10) returns for a cart with one item of 1000 cents, and why (at most 4 lines).

Facts you may use besides those reports (they are the call contract, not file contents): checkout reserves each [sku, qty] and throws 'out of stock <sku>' if reserve returns false; otherwise it returns cart.total(discountPct). Cart.total is applyDiscount(subtotal(items), discountPct) plus tax on that discounted subtotal. tax is Math.round(cents * 0.08). subtotal of one 1000-cent item is 1000. The discount argument here is 10. Do not open any source file. Reply with only the answer, at most 4 lines: the number returned and why.

contract.goal: From the Q1–Q3 reports only, state what checkout(cart, [['A1', 1]], 10) returns for a cart with one 1000-cent item, and why.
constraints: Use only the Q1, Q2, and Q3 reports that were added to this brief.
doneWhen: The report states the numeric return value of that checkout call and the reason, in at most 4 lines, using only the prior reports.

tasks.result:
## Outcome

Done. From the Q1–Q3 reports and the given call contract only, `checkout(cart, [['A1', 1]], 10)` returns **-9720**.

## Findings

`checkout(cart, [['A1', 1]], 10)` returns **-9720**.
`reserve('A1', 1)` succeeds (start stock 3 ≥ 1), so checkout returns `cart.total(10)`.
`applyDiscount(1000, 10)` is `Math.round(1000 * (1 - 10))` = **-9000** (`pct` is used as a fraction).
Tax on that is `Math.round(-9000 * 0.08)` = **-720**, so the total is -9000 + -720 = **-9720**.

## Verification

- Numeric return value and reason, at most 4 lines, using only the prior reports: met. Q1 gives `Math.round(cents * (1 - pct))`; Q3 gives `reserve('A1', 1)` true on the start map; the brief gives subtotal 1000, discount 10, and `tax = Math.round(cents * 0.08)` on the discounted subtotal. No source file was opened.

## Open issues

None.
